title: Shutdown stops consumer before draining its queue
evidence: stop() sets _stop_event before awaiting queue.join(); _worker loops only while that event is unset (line 366).
trigger: Call stop() with at least one queued event before the worker consumes it.
impact: Worker exits without task_done for pending items; stop() and their futures can wait indefinitely.

title: Encrypted retries cannot satisfy ledger idempotency
evidence: event_id derives from plaintext at 489-492; each retry encrypts anew at 496; existing ciphertext is compared byte-for-byte at 433.
trigger: Retry the same LedgerEvent with CORTEX_VAULT_KEY enabled.
impact: Randomized Fernet ciphertext differs, so an otherwise idempotent retry is rejected as a collision; nested rollback then terminates the worker.

title: Rollback is repeated after the transaction has already rolled back
evidence: _execute_insert_tx rolls back in its except block at 476-478; _process unconditionally rolls back again at 505 and closes the connection if that fails.
trigger: Any insert transaction error, such as a SQL CHECK constraint violation.
impact: The second ROLLBACK has no active transaction; the connection is closed and worker fails, leaving other queued futures unresolved. The collision path additionally rolls back at 434 before its exception handler rolls back again.

title: Attestation combines separate database snapshots
evidence: Counts and maxima are selected at 279-285, hashes at 287-289, without BEGIN; verify_chain opens another connection at 302.
trigger: Append commits between those reads while get_state_attestation runs.
impact: Reported totals, roots and integrity flag can describe different ledger states; anchor_to_rekor can publish an internally inconsistent head.

title: Manifest verification trusts the public key supplied by the manifest
evidence: Lines 173–177 read l0_public_key_b64 and signature from the same untrusted JSON; line 210 derives overall_valid without a pinned identity. Consumer bounty_cli.py:163–165 prints verified and returns success based on this boolean.
trigger: Supply a manifest signed by a newly generated attacker key, with status FROZEN_C5_REAL and omit optional db_path.
impact: The verifier reports an arbitrary self-signed manifest as a verified sovereign Aeon; integrity of a supplied signature is mistaken for authenticity. No protected runtime effect was traced.

title: Claim leaf encoding admits delimiter collisions
evidence: The five fields are joined with unescaped colons before hashing; (claim_id="a:b", advisory_id="c") and (claim_id="a", advisory_id="b:c") with identical remaining fields yield identical preimages.
trigger: Call exported compute_claim_leaf_hash with colon-containing identifiers.
impact: Distinct claim identities can share a leaf without breaking BLAKE3. Input validation at upstream ingestion was not established; scope is this public helper and verifier recomputation.

title: Unverified evidence status is accepted as verified citation
evidence: register persists record.status without restricting it; lookup returns any cache record; intercept patent/arXiv/DOI branches accept if record without checking status.
trigger: Register/load an EvidenceRecord with status REVOKED or UNVERIFIED and a 64-character nonempty digest, then intercept its citation under STRICT_ABORT.
impact: Citation passes strict enforcement, appears in verified_citations and contributes to a COMMITTED result despite its explicit unverified status.

title: Failed SQLite registration leaves evidence trusted in memory
evidence: register assigns self._cache[key] = record before opening and committing SQLite at lines 125-144; no rollback removes the cache entry on failure.
trigger: SQLite INSERT/connect fails, for example locked database or read-only database, and caller handles exception while retaining registry.
impact: lookup and interceptor accept evidence whose durable registration failed; current process and reopened registry disagree about trusted evidence.

title: Ledger model field reaches innerHTML without escaping
evidence: HUD lines 516-525 interpolate r.model_id into tbody.innerHTML. server.rs:118-139 accepts req.model and passes it directly to evaluate_and_seal; gate.rs:91-100 stores model.to_string() in recent_receipts. Router lines 53-62 show no route authentication layer.
trigger: A caller able to access the local chat endpoint submits a model string containing active HTML, then an operator opens or refreshes the ledger tab.
impact: Stored script-capable markup executes in the HUD origin and can read or modify the local UI and call same-origin endpoints. Static source trace only; no browser exploit executed.

title: HUD reports verified compliance from the existence of a response or receipt
evidence: The response badge hardcodes ESTADO: CONFORME EU AI ACT and ledger line 522 hardcodes VERIFICADO (ART. 12-14). No verification status is evaluated. gate.rs:97 likewise assigns a constant compliance string, and server.rs:146-198 generates formatted response templates.
trigger: Any chat response with choices, including the default model branch, or any receipt listed in the HUD.
impact: The interface presents a compliance verification as completed without displaying evidence or a verifier decision; scope is the UI claim, not a legal assessment.

title: Assimilation target can escape the incoming directory
evidence: CLI --target-name flows unchanged through assimilate_payload to INCOMING_DIR / target_filename and write_text at line 83; no containment validation.
trigger: Invoke assimilate with an absolute path or ../ segments naming an existing writable parent.
impact: The command overwrites files outside its documented incoming forge directory; no remote invocation or production authorization bypass is asserted.

title: Code fence extractor matches a literal backslash instead of a newline
evidence: The regex string contains four escaped backslashes before n, yielding a regex for a literal backslash followed by n rather than a line break. Fallback retains Markdown fences.
trigger: Normal remote output is ```python followed by a newline, Python code, and a closing fence.
impact: Python/JSON fenced responses fail syntax verification, while other extensions can be saved with fence markup intact.

title: Attestation verification accepts stale artifacts and an editable self-checksum
evidence: verify_attestation reads every digest from the same saved JSON and hashes those strings, comparing only to another field in that JSON (lines 167-176). It never calls compute_file_sha256, get_git_head_commit, or checks a signature. CLI main --verify directly consumes it and prints validity.
trigger: An input calendar/compliance file or Git HEAD changes after --emit, or a statement is edited and its unkeyed compound hash recomputed.
impact: The verifier reports VÁLIDA (100% Integridad Causal) despite changed source artifacts; it supplies no authenticated provenance.

title: Verification failures still return a successful CLI exit status
evidence: main calls verify_attestation() but ignores the returned boolean; both missing statement (False at line 161) and checksum mismatch (False at line 180) reach normal process termination.
trigger: Automation executes python tools/tamkarum_attestation_engine.py --verify on a missing or inconsistent statement.
impact: Shell/CI callers that check process status receive success even when verification failed.

title: Auto purge unlinks SQLite WAL files without checkpoint or connection coordination
evidence: Lines 23-24 delete all *.db-shm and *.db-wal recursively from cwd. strict_reviewer.py:155 calls run_auto_purge before git add/commit; no SQLite checkpoint or exclusive ownership is checked.
trigger: Strict reviewer or another caller runs purge while a database has committed WAL content not checkpointed into its main database.
impact: Committed database contents can be lost or concurrent clients disrupted; WAL files are persistent transaction state rather than disposable caches.

title: Receipt interpolation fails to escape JSON control characters
evidence: prompt/action/scope/agent only replace double quotes before interpolation into jsonResponse; backslashes and newlines are not JSON encoded.
trigger: An authorized invocation includes a multiline prompt or a path containing backslashes.
impact: Successful biometric signing emits malformed or altered JSON fields, causing receipt consumers to reject or misinterpret the result.

title: Curl failure can return the mail API key in error detail
evidence: Authorization bearer is embedded in cmd at lines 61–62. subprocess.run(check=True) raises CalledProcessError; when stderr is empty, str(e) includes the complete command. curl -s suppresses diagnostics, making the fallback relevant.
trigger: curl exits nonzero without stderr, e.g. a network failure under silent mode.
impact: Returned ERROR detail can disclose the bearer credential to callers or their logs.

title: Binary payload hash is truncated at the first NUL on read
evidence: payload_hash is ctypes.c_char * 16 (line 34); read accesses the structure field as a C string before bytes(...), although write stores arbitrary 16-byte digest data (80-81).
trigger: Write a digest whose first 16 bytes contain 0x00, then call read().
impact: The returned hash is shorter than the stored digest and loses its suffix, breaking digest round trips and comparisons.

title: Do not claim strict real-time determinism from one benchmark maximum
evidence: The only displayed evidence is one pair of aggregate benchmark results, yet lines 46-50 claim mathematical proof, strict real-time determinism, and patentability.
trigger: A reader relies on this audit as evidence of a worst-case timing guarantee or established patentability.
impact: A finite observed maximum does not establish a worst-case bound, nor do these results establish patentability. The document overstates the evidence and should qualify these conclusions.

title: Calibration resolves its technical corpus under scripts instead of the repository
evidence: root_dir is dirname(__file__)/.., which is scripts/. TECHNICAL_CORPUS_PATHS includes babylon60/database/core.py, strike_rs/src/atms.rs, README.md and AGENTS.md (21-27). The actual package is 01_KISH_ENGINE/babylon60 (pyproject.toml 103); scripts/AGENTS.md and scripts/strike_rs are absent, while scripts/README.md exists. Missing files only print warnings (63), and thresholds are still returned (77-84).
trigger: Run the calibration using the current directory layout, with its import dependencies available.
impact: The script calibrates from missing or unrelated inputs such as scripts/README.md and still emits final thresholds as if calibrated against the intended technical corpus.

title: Synthetic entropy demo presents label lookup as an empirical NLI comparison
evidence: Clustering compares supplied semantic_id labels, probe weights are random (56-58), yet measurements are labeled Oxford NLI clustering (263) and SEP acceleration (347).
trigger: Use run_empirical_stress_test output as comparative evidence about the cited semantic entropy or trained probe methods.
impact: The reported speedup measures integer label grouping versus a random linear projection on fabricated activations, so it does not validate the referenced NLI/probe implementations.

title: PROVED status certifies a fixed model unrelated to extracted preconditions
evidence: SELECT retrieves z3_precondition at 166 but never uses it. Every cluster instantiates the same template, with only a 16-character signature prefix and file count. The proof models poisoned/seq/writer checks (77-83), whereas codegen_rust_b60.py:127-142 emits only full signature/file-count checks, consuming PROVED rows at 41.
trigger: An EXTRACTED cluster passes the generated fixed Lean template.
impact: Database status PROVED and downstream generated verification comments imply evidence for an extracted rule and Rust correspondence that were never checked. This is a proof provenance gap; no effect authorization bypass is asserted.

title: Propagate failed and missing maintenance phases to the global verdict
evidence: Only phase_4 FAIL and phase_1 isolation FAIL set has_critical_failure. phase_2/3/5 failures become WARN; missing gates initialize True at 157-175. Lines 248-251 remove an existing alert when those two critical checks pass; line 318 returns zero.
trigger: Log preservation or vault consolidation fails, synchronization fails, or required gate scripts are absent.
impact: The scheduled command can report HEALTHY_OPTIMAL, clear an outstanding alert and exit successfully despite failed or unexecuted maintenance obligations.

title: Garbage collection totals count each target repeatedly
evidence: Twenty workers per cohort choose rules using sub_idx % len(rules); cohort rule counts are below twenty. Lines 155-159 sum every repeated scan into cohort and global totals without deduplication.
trigger: Any matching file in one of the configured targets.
impact: Reported file and byte totals are inflated by repeated workers, making cleanup capacity reports inaccurate.

title: Attestation generator emits unexecuted PASS results
evidence: test_data hardcodes copy_lint/link_checker/evidence_validator to PASS and fixed counts, then writes a fresh timestamp. The only executed subprocess in this generator is git rev-parse. Lines 71-87 also reuse fixed signature/hash/timestamp rather than binding the current commit and artifact digest.
trigger: Run the generator on any checkout, including one with failing gates or changed artifacts.
impact: The generated current-checkout evidence bundle contains fabricated gate outcomes and stale signing material, so it cannot support the claimed reproducible external verification. The manifest does state certification NONE and hardware UNVERIFIED, which does not qualify the PASS outcomes.

title: Attestation test passes even for blocked or failed results
evidence: The test branches only print status and errors at 24-29; it has no assertion about status, receipt or signature anywhere.
trigger: run_chaos_monad returns a failure/error dictionary without raising.
impact: The test succeeds and can give a false regression signal for a broken attestation pipeline.

title: Alarm batch discards its pending work before insertion succeeds
evidence: alarm() copies this.pending, sets it to [] and only then executes the INSERT (86-88). There is no restoration or durable queue.
trigger: The SQL INSERT throws, for example because processed_items is absent or a constraint rejects an item.
impact: Retry cannot recover the lost in-memory batch; the next callback sees an empty array and constructs INSERT ... VALUES with no rows. This is a defect in the published example, not a demonstrated production deployment.

title: Canonical annealing example replaces random acceptance with a fixed cutoff
evidence: The claimed Metropolis-Hastings criterion compares exp(-dE/T) to the constant 0.5 rather than a random uniform draw.
trigger: Use the documented canonical engine for optimization with repeated uphill proposals at a fixed positive temperature.
impact: Every uphill step above T*ln(2) is always rejected and every smaller step is always accepted; the example does not implement the stochastic acceptance it claims.

title: Merkle evidence seal does not bind field names
evidence: compute_merkle_root hashes only each value then sorts the leaf hashes at line 705; main stores this root as merkle_seal at 2935-2940.
trigger: Swap values of author and text, or rename evidence fields while retaining the multiset of values.
impact: Different evidence records have the same seal without a SHA-256 collision, undermining the advertised tamper evidence.
